## Measured · step 1 of Wanted · `domain:devx#1` · 2026-11-03T22:57Z

⛔ Not a claim yet (see the last line).

**Checkout duration per `Lint & Type Check` merge-group run** (12 `Checkout repository` steps each; seconds, from the jobs API `started_at`/`completed_at`):

| run created | conclusion | min | max |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| baseline, last run before 2026-11-01 | — | 39 | 163 |
| baseline, last run before 2026-11-02 | — | 41 | 60 |
| baseline, last run before 2026-11-03T12:00Z | — | 41 | 64 |
| 2026-11-03T21:32Z | failure | 62 | **1200** (the timeout) |
| 2026-11-03T21:52Z … 2026-11-03T21:59Z (5 runs) | success | 50–105 | 558–997 |
| 2026-11-03T22:31Z | success | 50 | 954 |
| 2026-11-03T22:40Z | success | 45 | 316 |
| 2026-11-03T22:48Z | in progress | 54 | 251 |

- **Where it hangs:** the timed-out job 126197313245 (run 41716369866, `Lint · docs & code guards`) spends the whole 20 minutes in one command, `git -c protocol.version=2 fetch --no-tags --prune --no-recurse-submodules origin +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/* +refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*` (`fetch-depth: 0`). Nothing before it is slow.
- **Ref counts now:** 1,514 heads and 17,361 tags on origin (`git ls-remote`), 218 of them `@18.3.0` tags from today's release. #22034 measured ~1,236 heads and ~7,950 tags when it was filed. Every `fetch-depth: 0` lane fetches all of them.
- **Reading:** the failures stopped, but the queue has **not** returned to baseline: the slowest checkout in each run is still 4–16 minutes against about 1–3 at baseline, so one slow fetch is still close to the 20-minute cap. The sudden onset at 2026-11-03T18:14Z points to a GitHub-side slowdown (githubstatus.com is not reachable from this session, so no incident link); the doubled tag count is the repository-side factor that makes every full fetch heavier and leaves less margin. Both are true at once, so step 3 alone does not close this card.
- **Stop-bleed (step 2), proposed shape for the dev:** keep the merge base the gates need, but stop fetching every head and tag on lanes that do not read them (for example a refspec limited to the PR head and `main`, or `filter: blob:none`), each lane's history need named from its own comment. That is `.github/workflows/**`, so Tier H with the maintainer's approval; and #22034 (`pm:on-hold`) is the same finding, so its `Restart-when:` is read before dispatch.

Next: this seat claims and dispatches step 2 under the p0 rule, unless the next two merge-group runs read every checkout under 180 s, in which case it records that and asks the maintainer to downgrade or close.

## Seat verdict · close · Wanted step 3 (GitHub-side) · `domain:devx#2` · 2026-11-06T01:48Z

Closing per Wanted step 3 and triage 6617501318 ("close this card with the evidence, or land the bounded checkout if the workflow is the cause"). The measurement (dev report 6674602390) shows the 2026-11-03 tail was a GitHub-side throughput loss. A bounded checkout with one retry does not lower the failure rate, so the stop-bleed this card was kept for has nothing to ship.

- **Seat re-check, not the report's account:**
  - Job 126213003280 (Test Core 5/8, ci.yml, no step timeout): `Checkout repository` ran 21:20:23Z → 22:07:45Z and then succeeded. That is a slow transfer, not a hang.
  - Job 126197313245 (`Lint · docs & code guards`): it failed at exactly 20:00 (20:51:16Z → 21:11:16Z).
  - The seat recomputed from the dev's raw job rows (ci.yml incident window, the four full-history jobs, n = 1666). P(> 20 min) = 1.56% and P(> 10 min) = 11.9%. P(> 20 min | > 10 min) = 13.1%, which is not below P(> 10 min). The hazard is flat, so restarting a fetch at 10 minutes buys nothing over letting it run.
  - The p50 is 267 s full-history against 47 s shallow (healthy: about 61 s against 22 s). Shallow fetches slowed too, so the platform was degraded for every checkout, not just the full-ref fetch.
- **What would help, and where it lives:** only a larger total budget or a smaller fetch. Raising the 20-minute CHECKOUT BUDGET to 25 on the 11 lint.yml lanes with wall room replays at 1.51% → 0.42%. That is a different change from this card's, and it breaks the one-budget rule `typecheck-source-gates` argues. Narrowing the fetch is #22034's direction B. Both are noted on #22034 for triage; neither is shipped here.
- **No change:** no branch was pushed, no PR, no workflow edit. The local branch `claude/issue-29980-bounded-checkout` is deleted with the worktree.
- If the 20-minute checkout timeouts come back, reopen this card or move #22034 under its `Restart-when:`.
